texts.preamble: Dinesh Kumar Verma & Anr vs North Dmc on 15 April, 2015 In The Court Of Ms. Shivali Sharma: Ascj: Central District: Tis Hazari Courts: Delhi Suit No. 427/14 In the matter of : Dinesh Kumar Verma & Anr. ......Plaintiff V E R S U S North Dmc ......Defendant Order
texts.facts: 1. Vide this order, I shall dispose off an interim injunction application u/o 39 Rule 1 & 2 CPC filed on behalf of plaintiffs against North DMC seeking restraint from creating any hindrance/obstruction in the peaceful use, enjoyment and possession of the plaintiffs and also from dispossessing the plaintiff from the suit property i.e. one Chabutra bearing Municipal No. 5628/2 on ground floor upto ceiling without roof rights measuring about 7'3" x 2'9" forming part of property no. 56285629 situated at Katra Jamunwala, New Delhi6 till the disposal of the present suit. 2. A suit for permanent injunction has been filed by the plaintiff seeking the same relief of injunction permanently on the pretext that plaintiff no.2 (wife of plaintiff no.1) is the owner of the suit property having purchased the same vide registered sale deed dt. 7.9.2010. There is an authorized electricity connection in the suit property and the same is also assessed to house tax. Plaintiff no.1 is running his business of selling kachories etc from the suit property since last more than 27 years under the name & style of 'J. B. Kachoriwala' and has received various awards and accreditation. 3. It is alleged that since the first week of September, 2014 the officials of the North DMC/defendant, without any rhyme or reason, have been harassing and torturing the plaintiff no.1 in one way or the other. On 05.09.2014, the officials of North DMC removed certain items of the plaintiff from the suit property and plaintiff no.1 was made to deposit the fine of Rs.1100/ for releasing the same. The officials of North DMC have been regularly visiting the suit property and creating unnecessary hindrance/interference in the smooth running of the business of plaintiff no.1 and have been threatening to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property illegally and forcibly. 4. Plaintiff no.1 had also made a representation dt. 25.09.2014 to the Chairman of North DMC to allow him to continue to carry on his business from the suit property. However, on 26.09.2014 the officials of North DMC again visited the suit property and threatened the plaintiff no.1 either to himself vacate the suit property within 3 or 4 days otherwise they will forcibly and illegally Dinesh Kumar Verma & Anr vs North Dmc on 15 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135036906/ 1 dispossess him from the suit property. Hence, the present suit has been filed. 5. WS has been filed on behalf of North DMC wherein the suit has been preliminarily objected to for want of statutory notice u/s 477/478 of DMC Act. On merits, it is stated that a complaint dt. 2.8.2014 was received by North DMC from Katra Jamun Cloth Merchant Association wherein they have alleged that they were worried because of the conduct of Dinesh Kachoriwala who had unauthorizedly occupied the main entrance and was carrying on the business of making kachories on the suit property for which he is using eatable oil for making the kachories and stove of kerosene oil. This is a small and narrow gate which leads to the cloth market and use of kerosene oil at the spot is a potential danger for any mishappening and in case of fire breaks out there may be heavy casualty and loss of property. On receipt of this compliant the Additional Commissioner (DEMS) vide letter no. PS/Addl. CM/NDMC/2014/D452 dt. 1.9.2014 directed the DHO, City Zone, Health Center to remove the kachoriwala within 24 hours and submit the ATR alongwith photographs. 6. Accordingly, an action was taken on 3.9.2013, during which a small counter, a stove, two drums of aluminum, two bhagona, one karai, one parat of aluminum, one Chhamni, two poni and one tank of steel were seized and after paying penalty the aforesaid items were released to the plaintiff. This action was taken because the plaintiff was encroaching the public land and was also preparing and selling the kachories from the site in question. Again an action was fixed on 19.9.2014 but the same could not be taken due to resistance of the mob. The site in question was again inspected by the concerned officials on 24.9.14, 29.9.2014 & 4.10.2014 and it was found that the kachories were being sold from the suit property. The plaintiff has no license to carry on the business from the site in question and as such his business activity is illegal and action against the same is under contemplation and will be taken as per law. In these circumstances, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed. 7. The copies of the complaint and order of DEMS has been placed on record by the North DMC.
